sections.content:
You know *es decir*, *o sea*, *en otras palabras*, *dicho de otro modo* and *mejor dicho* from B2 Unit 29. In academic prose a reformulation does one of four jobs. It restates an idea more simply or more exactly: *es decir*, *esto es*. It lists exactly what you have just announced: *a saber* ("namely"). It narrows or widens a term: *en sentido estricto*, *en sentido amplio*. And it corrects or softens a word you have just used: *mejor dicho*, *por así decirlo*.

Defining terms is the natural home of these markers. You choose a *término*, say what it names with *designar*, and narrow a topic down to one question with *acotar*.

sections.title: Four jobs, four markers
rows: El método es fiable; es decir, da siempre el mismo resultado.
The method is reliable; that is, it always gives the same result. (restates)
Hay dos tipos de sesgo, a saber, el de selección y el de medición.
There are two types of bias, namely selection and measurement. (lists exactly)
En sentido estricto, una muestra pequeña no prueba nada.
Strictly speaking, a small sample proves nothing. (narrows)
La muestra es pequeña, mejor dicho, demasiado pequeña.
The sample is small, or rather, too small. (corrects)

items.spanish: Usamos el término «sesgo» para designar un error que va siempre en la misma dirección.
items.english: We use the term "bias" to designate an error that always goes in the same direction.

items.spanish: En sentido amplio, el término «trabajador» incluye también a los estudiantes.
items.english: In a broad sense, the term "worker" also includes students.

items.spanish: Los resultados son claros; esto es, se repiten en las dos muestras.
items.english: The results are clear; that is, they repeat in both samples.

items.spanish: La muestra es, por así decirlo, la base del estudio.
items.english: The sample is, so to speak, the basis of the study.

sections.content: English speakers mix up "i.e.", "e.g." and "namely". *Es decir* is "i.e.": it restates. *Por ejemplo* is "e.g.": it gives one example. *A saber* is "namely": it gives the whole list, and comes after a general noun (*dos tipos, a saber…*). Also remember that *o sea* belongs to speech: in an essay, use *es decir* or *esto es*.
